text: ToF depth -> point cloud in tof_optical_frame (head TF from the pan/tilt joint states) -> ground/obstacle segmentation (cheapest proven equivalent of point_cloud_xyz + obstacles_detection) -> a spatio_temporal_voxel_layer in the Nav2 local costmap, with decay so stale voxels clear.
Nav2 collision_monitor gains a depth point-cloud source and a below-floor (cliff / negative obstacle) source.
Data published only when real ToF frames and TF exist (no placeholder data); obstacles marked only within the ToF's valid range and confidence.
Packages added to the node apt lists (STVL, rtabmap_util), configs, nav-stack static tests, READMEs; CPU measured on the robot before/after (Grafana/Mimir) within an agreed budget.
Web UI: obstacle voxels/cloud optionally visible in the 3D view; the agent can query nearby 3D obstacles.
2.5D: a ground robot that avoids 3D obstacles on the 2D map; no 3D path planning.
Onboard ToF obstacle perception on the Pi 5 feeding the Nav2 local costmap (3D obstacle layer) plus the collision monitor and cliff detection.
2.5D: ground robot avoiding 3D obstacles on the 2D map, no 3D path planning.
Head TF comes from the pan/tilt joint states.

The lidar map extends the ToF (and 3D SLAM) where possible: the lidar keeps its obstacle layer in both costmaps and its collision_monitor source alongside the new ToF sources (ToF adds 3D detail inside its 4 m view, lidar covers 360 deg / ~12 m beyond it); ToF clearing never clears lidar-marked obstacles outside the ToF frustum; when the 3D obstacle cloud is shown in the web UI 3D view, lidar points are shown with it.
